data.name: Cleo's Lost Idols
data.detailed_description:
Cleo’s Lost Idols is a unique and whimsical game in which players must restore Empress Cleopatra’s misplaced statues. Set in a comedy Ancient Egypt, this construction site chaos is the ultimate Sandbox game! Direct your workers by giving orders and manipulating physics obstacles: move boulders, push blocks, avoid fire traps and dodge the swinging spikes. Don’t let Cleopatra give you the Needle! Across 20+ tricky levels, there’s emergent gameplay and comedy outcomes to create: buildings to wreck, crates to smash, coins to collect, even a hot tub!

Your workers are, let’s be honest, a bit dumb – they forget where to go, get themselves burnt, drowned or even catapulted off the edge of the world! It’s your job to show them how to fulfil the Cleopatra’s wishes; keep on sending more of the little fellas until they do. Alternatively just smite them down with fire and lightning! It’s your management style, so your choice! The fate of the workers, their antics and even avoiding the clutches of Sobek the Crocodile God are all there to make us laugh.

Cleo’s Lost Idols has a deeply ingrained video mechanic, enabling you to make, edit, share and watch gameplay videos, right within the game; no video expertise required! Upload your videos to YouTube, get them liked, and watch yourself climb the rankings in the game’s video leaderboard. Enjoy other people’s clips too. Watch their workers fail to complete their orders in spectacular fashion, see their cunning solutions to getting the statue pieces restored, speed-run the levels or getting that last coin you didn’t even know existed.

Cleo’s Lost Idols is a strategy game about monumental construction in Ancient Egypt; not so much a pyramid scheme as an oasis of streaming fun as wide as the Nile!

data.short_description: Cleo's Lost Idols is a comedy sandbox physics game where you command workers to create mayhem! Emit fire and lightning, squirt water jets, push boulders and dodge fire traps whilst trying to find the missing statue pieces. There's an in-built video creator and tools to upload straight to YouTube.

reviews.review:
Cleo’s Lost Idols takes Ancient Egypt and transforms it into a playful physics-driven playground where construction, puzzle solving, and complete disorder regularly collide. Developed by Tomb Team and published by Chilled Mouse, the game approaches its historical setting with comedy rather than realism. Cleopatra’s missing statue pieces provide the basic motivation for the adventure, but the real attraction comes from attempting to control a workforce that has an impressive talent for getting itself into trouble. The result is a lighthearted combination of strategy, environmental puzzles, simulation, and slapstick entertainment.

Across more than 20 levels, the player is responsible for directing workers through increasingly hazardous environments while recovering pieces of Cleopatra’s statues. These workers are far from dependable. They can wander into traps, fall victim to environmental dangers, or otherwise turn a sensible plan into a spectacular failure. Instead of feeling like a conventional management game where commands are followed with mechanical precision, the experience encourages constant adjustment. Watching a carefully organized operation deteriorate into chaos is often just as entertaining as completing the objective successfully.

Environmental interaction plays an important role in keeping the levels interesting. Objects such as blocks and boulders can be manipulated to create routes or overcome obstacles, while hazards including fire and swinging traps force players to think about positioning and timing. Elemental abilities involving fire, water, and lightning add another layer of experimentation. These powers can contribute to practical solutions, but they are equally useful for creating amusing disasters when patience with the workforce begins to disappear.

The physics system is responsible for much of the game's personality. Objects and characters can interact in unpredictable ways, meaning that identical situations do not always feel completely predetermined. This creates an enjoyable sandbox quality in which experimentation becomes part of solving the puzzle. Players who appreciate controlled chaos may find themselves deliberately testing ridiculous ideas simply to discover what happens. The downside is that unpredictable behavior can occasionally become frustrating when success depends on workers cooperating with a carefully prepared plan.

Exploration offers additional distractions beyond the main objective. Coins can be collected, crates can be destroyed, structures can be damaged, and various environmental surprises encourage players to investigate each area. Even Sobek, the crocodile god, becomes part of the game's assortment of hazards. These elements help prevent the experience from becoming a simple exercise in moving workers from one location to another. There is usually some incentive to experiment with the environment or search for something beyond the most obvious route.

Another unusual feature is the game's emphasis on capturing the ridiculous moments created by its physics. Its video functionality was designed to allow players to record and edit gameplay sequences, making the numerous accidents, unusual solutions, and spectacular failures suitable material for short clips. This concept fits the game particularly well because unpredictable events are one of its biggest sources of entertainment. However, because the title dates back several years, players should approach older online and sharing-oriented functionality with modest expectations.

Visually, the colorful and cartoon-like presentation complements the comedic approach. This is not intended to be a historically accurate reconstruction of Cleopatra's Egypt. Instead, Egyptian imagery serves as the foundation for exaggerated environments, statues, traps, workers, gods, and physical comedy. The straightforward graphical style also helps keep important objects and hazards recognizable during moments when several things are happening simultaneously.

The overall depth is relatively modest compared with dedicated strategy, management, or construction simulations. There are tactical decisions to make and environmental puzzles to solve, but players looking for elaborate economic systems, sophisticated worker management, or extensive progression mechanics may find the experience limited. Its greatest strength lies in the interaction between simple objectives and unpredictable physics. That also means enjoyment depends heavily on tolerance for imperfect control. Players who become irritated when AI characters behave inefficiently may have a much harder time appreciating the joke.

Steam Deck users should consider the game playable rather than assume a completely optimized handheld experience. Compatibility information indicates that it can run on Steam Deck, but it should not be treated as equivalent to an official Steam Deck Verified designation. Its relatively straightforward mechanics make handheld play feasible, although occasional adjustments or minor interface inconveniences may be possible. Players specifically buying or installing games for Deck use should therefore expect functional compatibility rather than guaranteed console-like optimization.

As a free-to-play curiosity, Cleo’s Lost Idols offers an entertaining idea that is considerably more memorable than its modest production values might suggest. The combination of puzzle solving, worker direction, elemental powers, destructible surroundings, collectibles, traps, and chaotic physics gives the game an identity of its own. It can become repetitive and occasionally frustrating, but players who enjoy sandbox experimentation and watching carefully constructed plans collapse in ridiculous fashion can find plenty of amusement here.

It is an imperfect but creative physics puzzler whose strongest moments emerge from the unpredictable relationship between planning and disaster. Its limited strategic depth keeps it from reaching greater heights, yet its unusual Ancient Egyptian theme, mischievous mechanics, and willingness to embrace chaos make it an entertaining experience for the right audience.

Rating: 6/10
